BiblicalUsage: Machareshah is the mattock, the farmer's pick-axe, and it shows up in the days when Israel had no smith of their own and had to go down to the Philistines to sharpen every tool. The list in 1 Samuel 13:20 names the share, the coulter, the axe, and the mattock, and 1 Samuel 13:21 adds the file they used to keep those edges keen.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe even a sharpening file in this story preaches: when God's people lose the means to work and to fight, they end up dependent on their enemies.
